Musk Rages Against ‘Disney’s DEI Gestapo’ And Doubles Down On Crusade
By
Robert Hart
,
Former Staff.
Robert Hart is a former London-based Forbes senior reporter.
Feb 08, 2024, 08:44am EST
Feb 08, 2024, 09:10am EST
Share
Save
Topline
Tech billionaire Elon Musk tore into Disney and its CEO Bob Iger in a series of charged social media posts on Wednesday and Thursday, insulting the company’s recent content and slamming its diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives as he and
other billionaires clash
over the programs intended to boost worker value by fostering a more inclusive and equitable working environment.
Elon Musk criticized Disney's DEI program.
Getty Images
Key Facts
In a series of posts on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, Musk published what he claimed is Disney’s full set of DEI standards and guidelines on how to achieve them.
Musk savaged the guidelines, which he described as “laws,” as “racist, sexist” and “discriminatory” and the likely reason why most of the media giant’s content from the past few years “has sucked.”
The billionaire
said
the guidelines were “laboriously vile” and claimed merely navigating the “DEI minefield” will “crush the creative process.”
It “crushes the creative spirit of someone who just wants to make great art!,” Musk
said
in a response to a post from the Libs of TikTok, a
popular and influential account
known for its inflammatory posts and incendiary rhetoric against “liberals,” which often targets LGBT+ people.
Without providing any evidence, Musk said the company’s diversity programs are “enforced by Disney’s DEI Gestapo,” referencing Nazi Germany’s feared secret police, infamous for deploying brutal tactics and torture to suppress resistance.
News Peg
Musk’s tirade against DEI initiatives at Disney follows reports he is
supporting
actress Gina Carano in a lawsuit against the company. Carano was fired from Star Wars series “The Mandalorian” in 2021 for posting what Disney subsidiary Lucasfilm
described
as a series of “abhorrent and unacceptable” social media posts “denigrating people based on their cultural and religious identities.” The actress alleges discrimination and wrongful termination for airing her political views and exercising her right to free speech, a right she had used to
compare
the treatment of people with Republican views to the way Jews were treated in Nazi Germany. Musk encouraged people to join the lawsuit against Disney and seemingly
offered
legal support to people “discriminated against by Disney” or its subsidiaries like ESPN, Marvel and ABC.
Crucial Quote
“Walt Disney would despise Bob Iger,” Musk said. The comment followed an onslaught of social media posts
slamming
the Disney chief executive over the company’s decision to pull ads from X. Disney was one of many firms to pull advertising from the social media platform after Musk purchased it as Twitter in 2022 and rolled back content moderation, hate speech and verification policies intended to safeguard users.
Key Background
Disney
shares jumped
on Wednesday after the company issued its latest earnings report. Disney upped its guidance for the upcoming year, citing cost cutting and increased revenue from theme parks as key reasons for the improvement. The company told investors it’s on track to meet or exceed its $7.5 billion cost-cutting goal by the end of the fiscal year.
What To Watch For
Alongside its earnings, Disney also announced plans to stream an exclusive version of Taylor Swift’s Eras Tour concert movie on Disney+ and a $1.5 billion
partnership
with Epic Games, which makes the enormously popular game Fortnite. Iger
said
the moves would bring “significant growth” to the company and improve box office and streaming performance. Iger’s hope comes after a string of disappointing performances from its films over the past year, with new installations from its popular Marvel franchise failing to make the impact of earlier instantiations.
Contra
DEI programs have become a
point of contention
among some of the world’s most prominent titans of business. Musk has repeatedly slammed them as ineffective, counterproductive and tantamount to discrimination, especially against straight, white men. Hedge fund billionaire Bill Ackman has also railed against the “racist” initiatives, particularly at universities. Billionaire part-owner of the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks Mark Cuban has criticized Musk and Ackman for their opposition of DEI initiatives. Cuban defended the schemes as important ways of maximizing value from employees and helping companies understand their customers. Doubling down on his position, Cuban
challenged
his fellow billionaires to identify a top performing company that doesn’t have a DEI initiative. “Why do you think they have done so well in spite of their DEI programs,” he asked.
Forbes Valuation
We
estimate
Musk to be worth $198.2 billion. He is the world’s second richest person, a position he recently ceded to French luxury goods magnate
Bernard Arnault
, who is worth an estimated $214.7 billion. Musk is closely trailed by Amazon founder
Jeff Bezos
, who we estimate is worth $192.6 billion. A good deal of Musk’s wealth comes from a series of valuable, often futuristic, companies he cofounded and runs, notably electric carmaker Tesla and rocket firm
SpaceX
. He is also involved with brain implant enterprise
Neuralink
and tunneling firm Boring Company and controversially acquired Twitter, now X, in 2022 in the hopes of transforming it into a
trillion dollar
“
everything app
.”
